findings.title: Create storage error recorded as legacy duration
findings.body: In DualWriterMode3.Create, when Storage.Create fails the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) instead of d.recordStorageDuration. The timed interval is the storage call, not a legacy call, and no legacy call was made. Consequence: storage failures are invisible in storage metrics and falsely inflate legacy error metrics, hiding unified-storage outages.

findings.title: Update storage error recorded as legacy duration
findings.body: In DualWriterMode3.Update, when Storage.Update fails the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) instead of d.recordStorageDuration. No legacy call occurred on this path. Consequence: same as Create — storage update errors are misattributed to legacy, breaking alerts/dashboards for mode 3.

findings.title: Delete success records object name as kind label
findings.body: In DualWriterMode3.Delete success path the code calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) where name is the object name, while every other call passes options.Kind as the kind label. Consequence: per-object high-cardinality values pollute a Prometheus kind label, causing metric cardinality explosion and useless kind breakdowns.

findings.title: DeleteCollection legacy result recorded as storage duration
findings.body: In DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection the background goroutine calls d.Legacy.DeleteCollection but then calls d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy) instead of d.recordLegacyDuration. Consequence: legacy delete-collection latency/errors are never observed and are double-counted as storage, so legacy backup failures are invisible.

findings.title: Delete drops structured log values from context
findings.body: In DualWriterMode3.Delete the code builds log := d.Log.WithValues(name, kind, method) but then does ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) instead of using log. All other methods put the per-request log in the context. Consequence: request-scoped fields for delete are lost from downstream logs, hampering debugging.

findings.title: Async legacy backup inherits cancellable request context
findings.body: Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection all do go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...) ; d.Legacy.*(ctx, ...) } where ctx is the incoming request context. After the API handler returns the request context is cancelled, so the derived context is immediately Done and the 10s timeout does not help. Consequence: legacy backup writes described as a safe measure are routinely cancelled with context canceled, leaving legacy and unified stores diverged.

findings.title: Legacy async write reuses mutable input without copy
findings.body: In Create the code returns created to the caller while a goroutine concurrently reads obj, options and createValidation via d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, createValidation, options). Storage implementations commonly mutate obj in place and may alias created, creating a data race. Even without aliasing, legacy gets the pre-storage object without storage-assigned UID/resourceVersion. Update has the same flaw by re-invoking objInfo for legacy instead of reusing the storage result res, so legacy computes a different object from a different old state. Consequence: races/crashes under -race and persistent divergence between stores.

findings.title: Mode3 tests never verify async legacy writes
findings.body: TestMode3_Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection share one mock.Mock between legacy and storage mocks, return immediately without waiting for the background goroutine, and never assert legacy was called. The Create error case even registers the failure on setupLegacyFn while Storage.Create is the call that fails, passing only because the mock is shared. Consequence: a regression that stops the legacy backup write entirely would still pass, and unexpected background calls can panic after the test finishes.
